title: Pullback of an associated module sheaf
statement:
Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], put $R=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $S=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$, and regard $S$ as an $R$-algebra through $g^\sharp_X:R\to(g_*\mathcal O_Y)(X)=S$. For an $R$-module $M$ let $\mathcal F_M$ be the $\mathcal O_X$-module associated to $M$, with canonical section map $c_M:M\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_M)$ and, for $R$-linear $u:M\to M'$, the induced $\mathcal F_u:\mathcal F_M\to\mathcal F_{M'}$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-module]; likewise $\mathcal F_N$, $c_N$ on $Y$ for $S$-modules $N$. Let $g^*\dashv g_*$ be the pullback and pushforward of modules [def-pc-module-pullback], with unit $\eta$, and for $t\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal G)$ write $g^*t=\eta_{\mathcal G,X}(t)\in\Gamma(X,g_*g^*\mathcal G)=\Gamma(Y,g^*\mathcal G)$. Let $S\otimes_RM$ be the base change [def-weil-module-base-change]. Then there is exactly one morphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] $\theta_M:g^*\mathcal F_M\to\mathcal F_{S\otimes_RM}$ with
$$\theta_{M,Y}\bigl(g^*c_M(m)\bigr)=c_{S\otimes_RM}(1\otimes m)\qquad\text{for all }m\in M;$$
$\theta_M$ is an isomorphism, and it is natural in $M$: for every $R$-linear $u:M\to M'$, $\theta_{M'}\circ g^*(\mathcal F_u)=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{id}_S\otimes u}\circ\theta_M$. (Stacks, Modules, Lemma 01BJ, for schemes.)

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BJ (lemma-restrict-quasi-coherent), including its proof via the ringed-space pullback construction and the tensor extension of scalars

proof.text: The ring map and module structures. By definition of a morphism of ringed spaces [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], $g^\sharp:\mathcal O_X\to g_*\mathcal O_Y$ gives on global sections the ring map $g^\sharp_X:R=\mathcal O_X(X)\to\mathcal O_Y(g^{-1}X)=\mathcal O_Y(Y)=S$, which makes $S$ an $R$-algebra. For an $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal H$ the pushforward has $(g_*\mathcal H)(U)=\mathcal H(g^{-1}U)$ with $\mathcal O_X(U)$ acting through $g^\sharp_U$ [def-pc-module-pullback]; so $\Gamma(X,g_*\mathcal H)=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H)$, and its $R$-module structure is the $S$-module structure of $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H)$ restricted along $g^\sharp_X$. For an $\mathcal O_Y$-linear $\beta:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H'$, $(g_*\beta)_X=\beta_Y$.

Modules, Lemma 01BJ (lemma-restrict-quasi-coherent), proof: F_M = pi^*M (Lemma 01BH (1)) and the square of ringed spaces with ({*}, R), ({*}, S); Sheaves, Lemma 0097 (push-pull-composition-modules), whose proof is pushforwards compose plus uniqueness of adjoints; here unwound into hom bijections, pi_* being Gamma

proof.text: Existence and isomorphism. By Step 2 the bijections $\Phi_{\mathcal H}:\operatorname{Hom}(A,\mathcal H)\to\operatorname{Hom}(B,\mathcal H)$ are natural in $\mathcal H$ in the category of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, so by [lem-weil-pbc-coyoneda-iso-of-natural-hom-bijection] $\kappa=\Phi_A(\mathrm{id}_A):B\to A$ is an isomorphism with $\Phi_{\mathcal H}(\psi)=\psi\circ\kappa$. Put $\theta_M=\kappa^{-1}:g^*\mathcal F_M\to\mathcal F_{S\otimes_RM}$. The characterization of Step 2 for $\psi=\mathrm{id}_A$ gives $\kappa_Y(c_{S\otimes_RM}(1\otimes m))=g^*c_M(m)$, i.e. $\theta_{M,Y}(g^*c_M(m))=c_{S\otimes_RM}(1\otimes m)$ for all $m\in M$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BJ (lemma-restrict-quasi-coherent), proof: F_M = pi^*M (Lemma 01BH (1)) and the square of ringed spaces with ({*}, R), ({*}, S); Sheaves, Lemma 0097 (push-pull-composition-modules), whose proof is pushforwards compose plus uniqueness of adjoints; here unwound into hom bijections, pi_* being Gamma

proof.text: Uniqueness. If $\theta':g^*\mathcal F_M\to\mathcal F_{S\otimes_RM}$ is $\mathcal O_Y$-linear with $\theta'_Y(g^*c_M(m))=c_{S\otimes_RM}(1\otimes m)$ for all $m$, then $\theta'$ and $\theta_M$ have the same image $m\mapsto c_{S\otimes_RM}(1\otimes m)$ under the injective map $\psi\mapsto(m\mapsto\psi_Y(g^*c_M(m)))$ of Step 2 (with $\mathcal H=\mathcal F_{S\otimes_RM}$), so $\theta'=\theta_M$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BJ (lemma-restrict-quasi-coherent), proof: F_M = pi^*M (Lemma 01BH (1)) and the square of ringed spaces with ({*}, R), ({*}, S); Sheaves, Lemma 0097 (push-pull-composition-modules), whose proof is pushforwards compose plus uniqueness of adjoints; here unwound into hom bijections, pi_* being Gamma

proof.text: Naturality in $M$. Let $u:M\to M'$ be $R$-linear. The two $\mathcal O_Y$-linear maps $\theta_{M'}\circ g^*(\mathcal F_u)$ and $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{id}_S\otimes u}\circ\theta_M$ from $g^*\mathcal F_M$ to $\mathcal F_{S\otimes_RM'}$ agree on the sections $g^*c_M(m)$: naturality of the unit $\eta$ of $g^*\dashv g_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback] gives $(g^*\mathcal F_u)_Y(g^*c_M(m))=g^*(\mathcal F_{u,X}(c_M(m)))=g^*c_{M'}(u(m))$ by $\mathcal F_{u,X}\circ c_M=c_{M'}\circ u$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-module], which $\theta_{M'}$ sends to $c_{S\otimes_RM'}(1\otimes u(m))$ (Step 3); and $\theta_M$ sends $g^*c_M(m)$ to $c_{S\otimes_RM}(1\otimes m)$, which $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{id}_S\otimes u}$ sends to $c_{S\otimes_RM'}((\mathrm{id}_S\otimes u)(1\otimes m))=c_{S\otimes_RM'}(1\otimes u(m))$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-module], [def-weil-module-base-change]. By the injectivity of Step 2 (for $\mathcal H=\mathcal F_{S\otimes_RM'}$) the two maps are equal.
